question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) (Fifth Amendment) Regulations, 2024 (w.e.f. Nov 18, 2024), investors in an AIF scheme shall have rights PRO-RATA to their commitments, with limited exceptions. Which of the following is NOT a valid exception to the pro-rata-rights rule?

answer.text: Investor has been excused/excluded from participating in the investment
Investor has defaulted on providing pro-rata contribution for the investment
Performance Fees/Carried Interest shared with Investment Manager per Contribution Agreement
A preferred investor receiving priority loss-absorption over other classes (classical priority-distribution model)

explanation.text: The Logic: The Fifth Amendment allows pro-rata exceptions only for: (i) excused/excluded investor; (ii) defaulting investor; (iii) performance-fee/carry sharing with manager. The classical PRIORITY DISTRIBUTION model — where one class absorbs more loss than pro-rata so others get priority — is PROHIBITED post-Nov 18, 2024 for fresh commitments/new investments. The Trap: Options A, B, C are explicit carve-outs. Option D is what was killed off. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-D test Fifth Amendment. XIX-E reads it through the Cat III hedge-fund lens — junior units may still be subscribed by Manager/Sponsor/DFIs/sovereign entities. Manager's Pro-Tip: Junior/subordinate class is still allowed for Manager/Sponsor, DFIs, SIDCs, sovereign entities, central banks. Use this to absorb tail losses without running afoul of priority-distribution prohibition.
